09-16.title: B.B. King
09-16.description: Blues guitarist universally revered as the King of the Blues, whose expressive vibrato defined the sound of the electric guitar.

09-16.title: Marc Anthony
09-16.description: American salsa and Latin pop superstar who holds the record for best-selling tropical salsa artist of all time.

09-16.title: Nick Cave
09-16.description: Australian singer-songwriter and author whose dark, literary songcraft with the Bad Seeds spans five decades of powerful music.

09-16.title: Malaysia Founded
09-16.description: The Federation of Malaysia was formed, uniting Malaya, Singapore, Sabah, and Sarawak into a new nation.

09-16.title: Mexican Independence Day
09-16.description: Miguel Hidalgo's Grito de Dolores rang out at dawn, sparking Mexico's war of independence from Spain.

09-16.title: "The Thrill Is Gone" — B.B. King
09-16.description: B.B. King's signature recording features his beloved guitar Lucille weeping over a lush string arrangement in a blues masterpiece.

09-16.title: My Left Foot
09-16.description: Daniel Day-Lewis won his first Oscar for his shattering portrayal of Irish artist Christy Brown, who painted with his only controllable limb.

09-17.title: Hank Williams
09-17.description: Country music pioneer whose anguished honky-tonk songwriting on 'Your Cheatin' Heart' and 'Hey Good Lookin'' shaped all of American popular music.

09-17.title: Anastasia Romanov
09-17.description: Youngest daughter of Tsar Nicholas II whose fate after the Russian Revolution spawned decades of legend and imposters.

09-17.title: Baz Luhrmann
09-17.description: Australian director known for his maximalist visual style in Moulin Rouge!, Strictly Ballroom, and the 2013 Great Gatsby.

09-17.title: U.S. Constitution Signed
09-17.description: Delegates to the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia signed the U.S. Constitution, establishing the framework of American government.

09-17.title: Camp David Accords Signed
09-17.description: Egypt's Anwar Sadat and Israel's Menachem Begin signed the Camp David Accords brokered by President Carter, leading to a historic peace treaty.

09-17.title: "Your Cheatin' Heart" — Hank Williams
09-17.description: Hank Williams recorded this tearful country classic just months before his death at 29, leaving behind one of music's most haunting legacies.

09-17.title: Moulin Rouge!
09-17.description: Baz Luhrmann's dazzling jukebox musical set in 1900s Paris made Nicole Kidman and Ewan McGregor global stars and won two Oscars.

09-18.title: Jimi Hendrix
09-18.description: American guitarist who revolutionized rock music with his psychedelic playing and incendiary live performances before dying at 27.

09-18.title: Lance Armstrong
09-18.description: American cyclist who won seven consecutive Tour de France titles — later stripped due to doping — after surviving testicular cancer.

09-18.title: James Gandolfini
09-18.description: American actor whose portrayal of mob boss Tony Soprano in The Sopranos is widely considered the greatest performance in television history.

09-18.title: U.S. Air Force Established
09-18.description: The United States Air Force was established as an independent branch of the military under the National Security Act.

09-18.title: Jimi Hendrix Dies
09-18.description: Guitar legend Jimi Hendrix died in London at age 27, leaving behind a seismic musical legacy and the eternal question of what might have been.

09-18.title: "Purple Haze" — Jimi Hendrix
09-18.description: Hendrix's psychedelic debut single, introduced with one of rock's most iconic riffs, announced the arrival of a once-in-a-generation talent.

09-18.title: The Sopranos — Pilot
09-18.description: David Chase's groundbreaking HBO series about a New Jersey mob boss in therapy premiered and immediately redefined prestige television.

09-19.title: Jeremy Irons
09-19.description: British actor who won an Oscar for Reversal of Fortune and brought chilling menace to roles from Die Hard with a Vengeance to The Lion King.

09-19.title: Jimmy Fallon
09-19.description: American comedian and host of The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, known for his celebrity games and musical impressions.

09-19.title: Joan Lunden
09-19.description: American TV host who anchored Good Morning America for nearly two decades and became a trusted face in American living rooms.

09-19.title: Émile Zola Publishes 'J'Accuse'
09-19.description: Though the Dreyfus Affair started in 1894, Zola's open letter defending wrongly convicted Captain Dreyfus became one of history's most famous acts of public intellectualism.

09-19.title: Otzi the Iceman Discovered
09-19.description: Hikers in the Alps stumbled upon the 5,300-year-old frozen mummy of a Copper Age man, the oldest natural human mummy in Europe.

09-19.title: "All I Wanna Do" — Sheryl Crow
09-19.description: Sheryl Crow's breezy debut single about a lazy afternoon drinking became a summer anthem and launched one of pop's most durable careers.

09-19.title: The Lion King
09-19.description: Disney's animated Hamlet-inspired epic about a lion cub's journey to reclaim his kingdom became the highest-grossing film of 1994.

09-20.title: Sophia Loren
09-20.description: Italian cinema icon whose beauty and talent made her one of the greatest actresses in film history, winning the first acting Oscar for a foreign-language performance.

09-20.title: George R.R. Martin
09-20.description: American novelist and creator of the A Song of Ice and Fire series, the basis for HBO's Game of Thrones.

09-20.title: Jon Bernthal
09-20.description: American actor known for playing Shane Walsh in The Walking Dead and Frank Castle in Marvel's The Punisher.

09-20.title: Battle of the Sexes Tennis Match
09-20.description: Billie Jean King crushed Bobby Riggs in the famous Battle of the Sexes tennis match before 90 million television viewers worldwide.

09-20.title: Space Shuttle Discovery Lands at Dulles
09-20.description: The retired Space Shuttle Discovery made its final flight atop a modified 747, landing at Dulles International Airport for museum display.

09-20.title: "The Way" — Fastball
09-20.description: Fastball's mysterious road-trip anthem about an elderly couple who wandered away and died became an unexpected radio phenomenon.

09-20.title: Battle of the Sexes
09-20.description: Emma Stone and Steve Carell dramatized the legendary 1973 tennis showdown between Billie Jean King and Bobby Riggs.

09-21.title: Stephen King
09-21.description: Prolific American author of horror fiction whose works — from The Shining to It — have sold over 350 million copies.

09-21.title: Bill Murray
09-21.description: American actor and comedian who defined deadpan cool in Ghostbusters, Groundhog Day, and a string of Wes Anderson films.

09-21.title: Nicole Richie
09-21.description: American television personality, fashion designer, and actress who rose to fame on The Simple Life alongside Paris Hilton.

09-21.title: International Day of Peace
09-21.description: The United Nations established September 21 as the International Day of Peace, observed globally as a day of ceasefire and non-violence.

09-21.title: The Hobbit Published
09-21.description: J.R.R. Tolkien's The Hobbit was published by Allen and Unwin, launching the world's most beloved fantasy mythology.

09-21.title: "September" — Earth, Wind and Fire
09-21.description: Earth, Wind and Fire's joyous funk masterpiece — asking if you remember the 21st night of September — became one of music's most infectious songs.

09-21.title: It
09-21.description: The adaptation of Stephen King's novel about Pennywise the Dancing Clown became the highest-grossing horror film in cinema history.

09-22.title: Tom Felton
09-22.description: British actor who made Draco Malfoy one of Harry Potter's most compelling antagonists across eight blockbuster films.

09-22.title: Andrea Bocelli
09-22.description: Italian classical tenor who became the best-selling solo artist in classical music history despite losing his sight at age 12.

09-22.title: Billie Piper
09-22.description: British pop star turned acclaimed actress who played the first companion of the revived Doctor Who series.

09-22.title: Lincoln Issues Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation
09-22.description: President Lincoln announced that enslaved people in Confederate states would be declared free as of January 1, 1863.

09-22.title: Lost Premieres on ABC
09-22.description: The pilot of Lost aired — one of the most expensive in TV history — hooking 18.6 million viewers and launching a global phenomenon.

09-22.title: "Time to Say Goodbye" — Andrea Bocelli & Sarah Brightman
09-22.description: This soaring Italian operatic duet became one of the best-selling singles of all time, particularly in Germany.

09-22.title: Schindler's List
09-22.description: Steven Spielberg's black-and-white Holocaust masterpiece about Oskar Schindler saving 1,100 Jews won seven Oscars including Best Picture.

09-23.title: Bruce Springsteen
09-23.description: The Boss — American rock icon whose blue-collar anthems like Born to Run and Born in the USA defined working-class rock and roll.

09-23.title: Ray Charles
09-23.description: Blind American musical genius who fused gospel, blues, and country into soul music, earning the title 'The Genius.'

09-23.title: Jason Alexander
09-23.description: American actor and comedian best known as the neurotic George Costanza on Seinfeld, one of TV's most beloved sitcoms.

09-23.title: Neptune Discovered
09-23.description: Astronomers Johann Galle and Heinrich d'Arrest became the first to observe Neptune, the eighth planet, predicted mathematically before it was seen.

09-23.title: Google Celebrates Its Birthday
09-23.description: Google celebrates its founding on September 23 in some years, reflecting the ambiguous official founding date between September 4 and 27, 1998.

09-23.title: Born to Run — Bruce Springsteen
09-23.description: Springsteen's third album and his commercial breakthrough captures the desperate yearning of American youth in a wall of sound.

09-23.title: Ray
09-23.description: Jamie Foxx won the Academy Award for his transformative performance as Ray Charles in this sweeping biopic of the musical legend.

09-24.title: F. Scott Fitzgerald
09-24.description: American novelist and chronicler of the Jazz Age whose masterpiece The Great Gatsby remains one of the defining American novels.

09-24.title: Jim Henson
09-24.description: American puppeteer and creative genius who gave the world the Muppets, Kermit the Frog, and Sesame Street.

09-24.title: Pia Mia
09-24.description: American singer from Guam who rose to fame via social media before signing with Interscope Records and collaborating with Chris Brown.

09-24.title: Black Friday — U.S. Gold Market Crashes
09-24.description: Speculators Jay Gould and James Fisk tried to corner the gold market, causing a catastrophic financial panic on Wall Street.

09-24.title: India's Mars Orbiter Mission Enters Orbit
09-24.description: India's Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) successfully entered Martian orbit, making India the first Asian country to reach Mars.

09-24.title: "Rainbow Connection" — Kermit the Frog
09-24.description: Jim Henson's heartfelt ballad performed by Kermit the Frog in The Muppet Movie became a beloved ode to dreamers everywhere.

09-24.title: The Great Gatsby
09-24.description: Baz Luhrmann's lavish adaptation of F. Scott Fitzgerald's Jazz Age novel starred Leonardo DiCaprio as the enigmatic Jay Gatsby.

09-25.title: Will Smith
09-25.description: American actor and rapper who became one of Hollywood's biggest stars through Bad Boys, Men in Black, and Ali.

09-25.title: Mark Hamill
09-25.description: American actor who immortalized Luke Skywalker in Star Wars and became equally beloved as the Joker's voice actor in Batman: The Animated Series.

09-25.title: Michael Douglas
09-25.description: American actor and producer who won Oscars for One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (producer) and Wall Street (actor).

09-25.title: First American Woman Walks in Space
09-25.description: Astronaut Kathryn Sullivan became the first American woman to perform a spacewalk during the Space Shuttle Challenger mission STS-41-G.

09-25.title: Nirvana's Nevermind Released
09-25.description: Nirvana's landmark second album arrived and within weeks had knocked Michael Jackson off the Billboard charts, signaling grunge's mainstream arrival.

09-25.title: Nevermind — Nirvana
09-25.description: Nirvana's world-changing second album, featuring 'Smells Like Teen Spirit,' killed hair metal overnight and defined Generation X.

09-25.title: Wall Street
09-25.description: Oliver Stone's searing portrait of 1980s greed features Michael Douglas's Oscar-winning turn as Gordon Gekko declaring 'Greed is good.'

09-26.title: T.S. Eliot
09-26.description: Anglo-American poet who wrote The Waste Land, considered the most important poem of the 20th century.

09-26.title: Olivia Newton-John
09-26.description: British-Australian singer and actress whose role as Sandy in Grease made her an icon, and whose 'Physical' dominated 1981.

09-26.title: Serena Williams
09-26.description: American tennis player widely considered the greatest of all time, with 23 Grand Slam singles titles and an incomparable career.

09-26.title: The Beatles Make Their TV Debut
09-26.description: The Beatles appeared on Granada TV's People and Places, beginning a TV presence that would electrify Britain and then the world.

09-26.title: Nuclear War Almost Starts — Soviet False Alarm
09-26.description: Soviet officer Stanislav Petrov correctly identified a nuclear missile warning as a false alarm, possibly preventing World War III.

09-26.title: "Physical" — Olivia Newton-John
09-26.description: Olivia Newton-John's synth-pop workout anthem spent ten weeks at No. 1 in the U.S. — the longest reign of the entire decade.

09-26.title: The West Side Story
09-26.description: Robert Wise and Jerome Robbins' Romeo and Juliet musical set in New York's street gangs won ten Academy Awards.

09-27.title: Avril Lavigne
09-27.description: Canadian punk-pop singer-songwriter whose debut album Let Go became one of the best-selling albums of the 21st century.

09-27.title: Lil Wayne
09-27.description: American rapper from New Orleans who dominated hip-hop in the late 2000s with mixtapes that influenced a generation of artists.

09-27.title: Meat Loaf
09-27.description: American rock singer whose Bat Out of Hell, featuring operatic bombast co-written with Jim Steinman, is one of the best-selling albums ever.

09-27.title: Cabrillo Discovers California
09-27.description: Portuguese explorer Juan Rodriguez Cabrillo became the first European to set foot on the coast of what is now California.

09-27.title: The Warren Commission Report Released
09-27.description: The Warren Commission published its report concluding that Lee Harvey Oswald acted alone in the assassination of President Kennedy.

09-27.title: "Sk8er Boi" — Avril Lavigne
09-27.description: Avril Lavigne's pop-punk anthem about social class and missed connections became a defining song of early-2000s youth culture.

09-27.title: A Beautiful Mind
09-27.description: Ron Howard's biopic of Nobel-winning mathematician John Nash, played by Russell Crowe, won four Academy Awards including Best Picture.

09-28.title: Confucius
09-28.description: Chinese philosopher whose teachings on ethics, family loyalty, and social harmony shaped East Asian civilization for 2,500 years.

09-28.title: Naomi Watts
09-28.description: British-Australian actress who earned an Oscar nomination for 21 Grams and became a horror icon in The Ring.

09-28.title: Dita Von Teese
09-28.description: American burlesque performer and model who single-handedly revived the art of neo-burlesque as a sophisticated entertainment form.

09-28.title: Penicillin Discovered by Alexander Fleming
09-28.description: Alexander Fleming noticed that mold had contaminated his petri dish and killed bacteria, leading to the discovery of penicillin.

09-28.title: Brigitte Bardot Born
09-28.description: French actress and model Brigitte Bardot was born on this date, becoming the defining sex symbol of post-war Europe.

09-28.title: "Toxygene" — The Orb
09-28.description: The Orb's ambient techno epic became a surprise UK No. 4 hit, bringing electronic music into the mainstream charts.

09-28.title: The Ring
09-28.description: Gore Verbinski's American remake of the Japanese horror classic Ringu terrified audiences with its cursed videotape premise.

09-29.title: Lech Walesa
09-29.description: Polish labor activist and Nobel Peace Prize laureate who led the Solidarity trade union movement that helped end Communist rule in Poland.

09-29.title: Sebastian Bach
09-29.description: Canadian rock vocalist and Skid Row frontman whose powerhouse voice made 18 and Life and I Remember You metal classics.

09-29.title: Anita Ekberg
09-29.description: Swedish actress immortalized by Federico Fellini in the Trevi Fountain scene of La Dolce Vita, one of cinema's most iconic images.

09-29.title: Dow Jones Drops 778 Points — Largest Single-Day Drop
09-29.description: The U.S. House of Representatives rejected the $700 billion bailout bill, triggering the largest single-day point drop in Dow Jones history.

09-29.title: The Tylenol Murders
09-29.description: Seven people in Chicago died after taking cyanide-laced Tylenol capsules, triggering a national panic and forever changing product packaging.

09-29.title: "18 and Life" — Skid Row
09-29.description: Skid Row's power ballad about a troubled teen's fatal mistake launched Sebastian Bach's voice onto rock radio and MTV worldwide.

09-29.title: La Dolce Vita
09-29.description: Federico Fellini's sprawling meditation on celebrity, decadence, and emptiness in 1960s Rome remains a touchstone of world cinema.

09-30.title: Truman Capote
09-30.description: American author who wrote Breakfast at Tiffany's and the nonfiction novel In Cold Blood, a landmark work of literary journalism.

09-30.title: Martina Hingis
09-30.description: Swiss tennis prodigy who became the youngest Grand Slam singles champion and world No. 1 in tennis history.

09-30.title: Eric Stoltz
09-30.description: American actor best known for his role as Rocky Dennis in Mask and his brief casting as Marty McFly before being replaced by Michael J. Fox.

09-30.title: James Dean Dies in Car Crash
09-30.description: Hollywood icon James Dean was killed in a car crash near Cholame, California at age 24, cementing his status as the ultimate symbol of rebellious youth.

09-30.title: Monica Lewinsky Scandal — Starr Report Released
09-30.description: Kenneth Starr's 445-page report detailing President Clinton's affair with Monica Lewinsky was released to Congress and the internet simultaneously.

09-30.title: "Rebel Rebel" — David Bowie
09-30.description: David Bowie's glam rock farewell to Ziggy Stardust features one of rock's most instantly recognizable guitar riffs.

09-30.title: Breakfast at Tiffany's
09-30.description: Audrey Hepburn's iconic portrayal of Holly Golightly, based on Truman Capote's novella, defined a generation of style and yearning.
